title: QUIC RFC 9000 Zero-Length Connection-ID Mode Runtime Verification
verification_method: Focused requirement-home execution, protected 1-RTT packet opening for outbound DCID selection, nearby connection-ID lifecycle regression tests, solution build, SpecTrace validation, and diff hygiene.
scope: This verification covers local connection-ID issuance suppression after local zero-length selection and empty outbound Destination Connection ID selection for packets sent toward peers that selected zero-length mode. It does not cover public configuration APIs, multipath, broad migration success, or application-layer behavior.
expected_result: Requirement-home tests prove that local zero-length mode suppresses explicit and replenishment CID issuance, non-zero local mode still allows issuance, peer zero-length mode emits protected application-data packets that open only with an empty Destination Connection ID, and non-zero peer mode continues to use the non-zero destination ID. Nearby connection-ID lifecycle and zero-length migration guard regressions remain green.
procedure: Run focused requirement-home and regression tests for S5P1P1-0020, S5P1P1-0021, S5P1P1-0012, S5P1P1-0014, S5P1P2-0011, S9P5-0005, and S9P5-0010.
Open protected outbound application-data packets with empty and non-empty Destination Connection ID expectations.
preconditions: Local zero-length mode is represented by committed local transport parameters whose Initial Source Connection ID is present with length zero.
Peer zero-length mode is represented by peer transport parameters committed through runtime TLS state update events.
The runtime has 1-RTT packet protection material before outbound packet inspection.

supplemental_sections.heading: Packet Inspection Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: The outbound zero-length proof opens protected 1-RTT datagrams with an empty Destination Connection ID and verifies the same datagrams do not open with the old non-zero handshake destination ID.

status_summary: Passed for the bounded zero-length connection-ID mode runtime slice. Focused tests passed 19/19 after the runtime began installing empty outbound DCIDs through peer transport-parameter commit and suppressing local CID issuance from committed local zero-length transport parameters.
